chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is permissible regarding witnesses in Mut'ah (temporary marriage)? He said: One man and two women. I said: If he dislikes [having] witnesses, he said: One man suffices for him, and that is due to the status of the woman, so that she does not say in herself, 'This is fornication.'
ai.seo_question: What are the witness requirements for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies that while the standard witness requirement for Mut'ah is one man and two women, a single male witness suffices if preferred, specifically to preserve the woman's dignity and prevent her from perceiving the union as fornication (fujur). This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the psychological and social perception of the woman in temporary marriage, distinguishing it from illicit relations through proper contractual visibility.
